options.summary: Seek to a position; bare values are seconds

variants.meaning: Seek position relative to the selected input/output timeline

platform.reason: This parameter definition does not select an operating system; platform availability is not asserted

forms.grammar: A signed decimal count of seconds
Hours, minutes and seconds; an optional leading minus sign is part of duration syntax, not a universal sentinel

options.detail: FFmpeg 7.1: accept signed decimal seconds, literal s/ms/us suffixes, or [-][HH:]MM:SS[.fraction]. For example, 200ms is 0.2 seconds. The option applies to an input before -i, or to an output before its URL. Syntax permitting a sign does not establish a special negative-value effect for every input/output mode.

categories.name: Stream codecs
categories.description: The colon selector is part of the option name. These entries specify all video or audio streams, or stream index zero. Other concrete selectors can be added to custom profiles.

references.locator: Generic codec option b: bitrate in bits/s

platform.reason: This parameter definition does not select an operating system; platform availability is not asserted

forms.grammar: Numeric target bitrate in bits/second; encoder constraints apply
The documented numerical-option grammar supports additional SI prefixes; i chooses binary scaling and B multiplies by eight. Encoder-specific accepted ranges/defaults remain applicable

when_absent.meaning: The selected encoder's default rate-control settings apply

options.detail: FFmpeg 7.1: bare numbers are bits/second. K or k, M and G use decimal powers of 1000; adding i selects powers of 1024, and a final B multiplies the value by 8. Thus 128k means 128000 bits/second, while 1MiB means 8388608 bits/second. Do not append /s. The selected encoder determines useful bounds, zero-value effects and defaults; zero is not universally an unlimited-rate sentinel.
